title: Wipro Launches STO360 With Aramco, SAP as Stock Slips Toward Nifty Exit
excerpt: Wipro's new STO360 platform, co-developed with Aramco and SAP, modernizes shutdown and outage management for asset-heavy industries — but the launch arrives as shares scrape a 52-week low and the company prepares to exit the Nifty 50 on September 30.
body:
• Wipro launched STO360 on September 17, 2026 — a cloud-native platform built on SAP's Business Technology Platform and co-developed with Aramco and SAP for shutdown, turnaround and outage management in asset-heavy industries.
  • STO360 has earned SAP Endorsed App status and is sold through the SAP Store, giving Wipro a repeatable, IP-led product aimed at SAP's global enterprise client base.
  • Wipro shares closed at ₹166.40 on Thursday, down 0.29%, and touched a new 52-week low of ₹164.40 on Friday — twelve days before the company's September 30 exit from the Nifty 50.
  • BSE Ltd replaces Wipro in the benchmark, the first exclusion in three decades, affecting roughly $97 billion in assets tracking the Nifty 50 and Equal Weight indices.

Wipro launches AI-led STO360 with Aramco and SAP

Wipro Limited on Thursday launched Wipro STO360, a digital solution developed with Aramco and SAP to modernize shutdown, turnaround and outage management for asset-intensive industries. Built on SAP's Business Technology Platform and targeting oil and gas, chemicals, mining, manufacturing and utilities, the cloud-native product gives plant operators real-time visibility into critical activities across the shutdown lifecycle.

STO operations — planned maintenance windows when plants halt production for inspections, repairs and upgrades — are among the costliest moments in an asset-heavy company's calendar, with poorly managed shutdowns costing millions of rupees a day in lost output. Wipro says STO360 improves coordination between teams, supports better-informed decision-making,.

"Asset heavy industries need to embrace AI-led transformation quickly and at scale due to the increasing complexity, regulatory expectations, and the need for operational excellence."

— Vinay Firake, CEO of APMEA, Wipro Limited

"The platform could help Aramco improve the efficiency and productivity of turnaround and inspection planning and execution."

— Ahmad O. Al Khowaiter, Executive Vice President of Technology and Innovation, Aramco

Context & Background

The launch deepens a relationship spanning more than two decades, with Wipro and Aramco having collaborated on IT, engineering and digital transformation initiatives linked to Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 program. Wipro said STO360 combines its industry expertise with its Wipro Intelligence AI capabilities and Aramco's operational leadership in running complex turnarounds.

Two commercial details matter beyond the announcement. STO360 has been recognized as an SAP Endorsed App, a designation reserved for premium partner solutions, and it is available through the SAP Store.

The launch lands in a busy fortnight. On September 15 Wipro announced an expanded Google Cloud partnership on enterprise AI, including plans to train more than ten thousand professionals in AI, and the company renewed its Digital Workplace Services contract with ABB earlier in September.

Impact & Analysis

The market response was muted. Shares closed at ₹166.40 on the NSE on Thursday, down 0.29% or ₹0.49, according to europesays, and touched a new 52-week low of ₹164.40 on Friday, undercutting the previous low of ₹165.02, LatestLY reported. The stock has declined more than 7% in a month and roughly 38% in 2026, according to Inshorts, against a 52-week high of ₹273.10.

The launch arrives twelve days before Wipro's exit from the Nifty 50. The NSE announced on August 10 that Wipro will be removed from India's benchmark index effective September 30, replaced by BSE Ltd. — the first exclusion in three decades apart from a brief interval in 2013 when Wipro demerged its non-IT businesses. The cause is mechanical: Wipro's six-month average free-float market capitalization of about ₹559.3 billion was less than half of BSE's ₹1.4 trillion, short of the methodology's requirement that an incoming constituent carry at least 1.5 times the smallest constituent's market value, according to Bloomberg's reporting. The change affects roughly $97 billion in assets tracking the Nifty 50 and Equal Weight indices, forcing index-tracking funds to sell.

It also reflects a sector under pressure. The top five Indian IT firms now account for less than 9% of the Nifty 50, the lowest share since at least 2002. Wipro's June-quarter results showed net income up just 0.6% year on year with revenue hurt by weak discretionary spending, and Morgan Stanley maintained a price target of ₹161 in June, expecting Wipro to lag peers in sequential growth.

Diaspora Angle

Wipro is a bellwether of the Indian IT model built on offshore delivery, and its Nifty exit marks the first time in three decades the benchmark has dropped one of India's original software giants.

What's Next

The commercial test is whether STO360's SAP Endorsed App status and SAP Store distribution win paying customers and deliver IP-led revenue to offset pressure on traditional services. September 30 brings the mechanical event — index funds rebalancing out of Wipro — and the December quarter will show whether AI-led products like STO360 and the Google Cloud Gemini partnership are converting into deal wins.
